title: Child is directly identifiable through continuous GPS sharing
description: By transmitting precise live GPS coordinates at regular intervals, the child may be directly or indirectly identifiable, especially when coordinates repeatedly map to home, school, or other unique locations tied to a specific child.
assumptions: The backend can associate the incoming GPS stream with an account, device, or session linked to the child.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for identifiability from shared content; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Location updates enable linkage of multiple observations to the same child
description: Regular interval GPS transmissions create a persistent movement pattern that allows multiple events and records to be linked to the same child over time, even if explicit identifiers are minimized.
assumptions: The flow includes stable metadata, timing, network, device, or account context sufficient to correlate successive updates.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for linkability across observations in transit; exact node id may differ in the official threat tree.

title: GPS coordinates reveal the child's identity through unique movement patterns
description: Even without a direct identifier in payload, precise and repeated location traces can single out the child because home/school routines and unique trajectories can identify an individual.
assumptions: An observer of the flow or a party with access to transmitted data can correlate traces with known addresses or routines.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an informed approximation for identifiability from data content and patterns.

title: Sensitive information is disclosed in transit via live location data
description: Live GPS coordinates disclose highly sensitive personal information, including current whereabouts and inferred habits, to any unauthorized party able to observe the transmission.
assumptions: Transport protection may be absent, weak, misconfigured, or endpoints/logging infrastructure may expose the data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for sensitive data in transit; exact numbering may vary.

title: Backend can link location history across sessions and contexts
description: On receipt, the backend can aggregate successive GPS updates into a longitudinal location history, linking the child's movements across time, sessions, and potentially other datasets.
assumptions: Backend stores or processes updates with persistent identifiers or account context.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for recipient-side linkage through aggregation; exact node id may vary.

title: Backend learns sensitive habits and places from stored location history
description: By processing and storing regular GPS updates, the backend can infer home address, school, religious attendance, medical visits, routines, and social relationships from the child's movement history.
assumptions: Backend retains sufficient historical data and has analytics capability.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit disclosure node for inference from received data; exact node id may vary.

title: Child may be unaware of the extent and frequency of location tracking
description: The backend's collection and use of live GPS updates may not be transparent to the child, creating a risk that the child does not understand when tracking occurs, how often data is sent, or how it is used.
assumptions: Notices are limited, not child-appropriate, or not presented at the moment of collection.
uncertainty_note: Node id is an informed approximation for insufficient awareness/transparency.

title: Collection of continuous child location data may exceed necessity or valid consent
description: Receiving live GPS coordinates at regular intervals from a child may be non-compliant if the collection is not necessary, proportionate, properly consented to by a parent/guardian where required, or governed by child-specific legal obligations.
assumptions: Applicable law or policy imposes heightened requirements for children's location data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact numbering depends on the LINDDUN Pro tree version and applicable jurisdiction.

title: Backend disclosure enables linking of location pings to the same user/device
description: By writing each location ping from the backend into the Location History Store, the source causes records to be accumulated under stable account, device, or session identifiers. This enables multiple pings to be linked together into a longitudinal movement profile for the same individual.
assumptions: Assumes each ping is stored with a persistent or quasi-persistent identifier, or can otherwise be associated with the same subject over time.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best-fit estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may differ.
